title: OSHA construction health hazards study guide
description: OSHA construction health hazards study guide: first aid, sanitation, noise, lasers, air contaminants, ventilation, lighting and lead, linked to 29 CFR 1926.
intro: Subpart D of OSHA's construction rules (29 CFR 1926.50 to 1926.66) covers occupational health and environmental controls. This guide sets out what the rule text states on medical services and first aid, sanitation, noise, lasers and microwaves, gases, vapors, fumes, dusts and mists, illumination, ventilation basics, the hazard communication pointer and the basics of the lead standard. Ionizing radiation, COVID-19, methylenedianiline, process safety management, HAZWOPER and spray booths are not covered. Consensus standards the rule names are only named here, not summarized. Every point links to the regulation and quotes its exact words.

points.text: The employer must make sure medical personnel are available for advice and consultation on matters of occupational health.
points.quote: The employer shall insure the availability of medical personnel for advice and consultation on matters of occupational health.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Provisions for prompt medical attention in case of serious injury must be made before the project starts.
points.quote: Provisions shall be made prior to commencement of the project for prompt medical attention in case of serious injury.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: If no infirmary, clinic, hospital or physician that is reasonably accessible in time and distance to the worksite is available to treat injured employees, a person with a valid first-aid training certificate from the U.S. Bureau of Mines, the American Red Cross, or equivalent training that can be verified by documentary evidence must be available at the worksite to render first aid.
points.quote: a person who has a valid certificate in first-aid training from the U.S. Bureau of Mines, the American Red Cross, or equivalent training that can be verified by documentary evidence, shall be available at the worksite to render first aid.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: First aid supplies must be easily accessible when required. First aid kit contents go in a weatherproof container with individual sealed packages for each type of item. The employer checks the kit before it is sent out on each job and at least weekly on each job so that used items are replaced.
points.quote: The contents of the first aid kit shall be placed in a weatherproof container with individual sealed packages for each type of item, and shall be checked by the employer before being sent out on each job and at least weekly on each job to ensure that the expended items are replaced.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Proper equipment for prompt transportation of the injured person to a physician or hospital, or a communication system for contacting necessary ambulance service, must be provided.
points.quote: Proper equipment for prompt transportation of the injured person to a physician or hospital, or a communication system for contacting necessary ambulance service, shall be provided.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Where 911 emergency dispatch services are not available, the telephone numbers of the physicians, hospitals or ambulances must be conspicuously posted.
points.quote: In areas where 911 emergency dispatch services are not available, the telephone numbers of the physicians, hospitals, or ambulances shall be conspicuously posted.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Where 911 is available and the employer uses a communication system that does not automatically give the 911 dispatcher the caller's latitude and longitude, the employer must post, in a conspicuous location at the worksite, either the worksite's latitude and longitude or other location information that communicates the worksite's location effectively to employees. This does not apply to worksites with readily available land lines whose 911 service automatically identifies the caller's location.
points.quote: When using a communication system in an area that does not automatically supply the caller's latitude and longitude information to the 911 emergency dispatcher, the employer must post in a conspicuous location at the worksite either:

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Where the eyes or body of any person may be exposed to injurious corrosive materials, suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body must be provided within the work area for immediate emergency use.
points.quote: suitable facilities for quick drenching or flushing of the eyes and body shall be provided within the work area for immediate emergency use.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.50, Medical services and first aid (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: An adequate supply of potable water must be provided in all places of employment.
points.quote: An adequate supply of potable water shall be provided in all places of employment.

points.text: Portable containers that dispense drinking water must be capable of being tightly closed and equipped with a tap. Water may not be dipped from containers.
points.quote: Portable containers used to dispense drinking water shall be capable of being tightly closed, and equipped with a tap. Water shall not be dipped from containers.

points.text: The common drinking cup is prohibited. Where single service cups are supplied, there must be a sanitary container for unused cups and a receptacle for used cups.
points.quote: The common drinking cup is prohibited.

points.text: Outlets for nonpotable water (such as water for industrial or firefighting purposes only) must be identified by signs showing the water is unsafe and not to be used for drinking, washing or cooking. There may be no cross-connection, open or potential, between potable and nonpotable water systems.
points.quote: There shall be no cross-connection, open or potential, between a system furnishing potable water and a system furnishing nonpotable water.

points.text: Table D-1 sets the minimum toilet facilities: 1 for 20 or less employees; 1 toilet seat and 1 urinal per 40 workers for 20 or more; 1 toilet seat and 1 urinal per 50 workers for 200 or more.
points.quote: 20 or less 1. 20 or more 1 toilet seat and 1 urinal per 40 workers. 200 or more 1 toilet seat and 1 urinal per 50 workers.

points.text: The toilet requirements of 1926.51(c) do not apply to mobile crews that have transportation readily available to nearby toilet facilities.
points.quote: The requirements of this paragraph (c) for sanitation facilities shall not apply to mobile crews having transportation readily available to nearby toilet facilities.

points.text: The employer must provide adequate washing facilities, near the worksite, for employees applying paints, coatings, herbicides or insecticides, or in other operations where contaminants may be harmful to employees.
points.quote: The employer shall provide adequate washing facilities for employees engaged in the application of paints, coating, herbicides, or insecticides, or in other operations where contaminants may be harmful to the employees.

points.text: Where a particular standard requires showers, one shower is provided for each 10 employees of each sex, or numerical fraction thereof, who must shower during the same shift.
points.quote: One shower shall be provided for each 10 employees of each sex, or numerical fraction thereof, who are required to shower during the same shift.

points.text: No employee may be allowed to eat or drink in a toilet room or in any area exposed to a toxic material.
points.quote: No employee shall be allowed to consume food or beverages in a toilet room nor in any area exposed to a toxic material.

points.text: Protection against the effects of noise exposure must be provided when sound levels exceed Table D-2, measured on the A-scale of a standard sound level meter at slow response.
points.quote: Protection against the effects of noise exposure shall be provided when the sound levels exceed those shown in Table D-2 of this section when measured on the A-scale of a standard sound level meter at slow response.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Above the Table D-2 levels, feasible administrative or engineering controls must be used. If they fail to bring sound levels within the table, PPE as required in Subpart E must be provided and used.
points.quote: feasible administrative or engineering controls shall be utilized. If such controls fail to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table, personal protective equipment as required in subpart E, shall be provided and used to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Table D-2 lists permissible exposures by duration per day: 8 hours at 90 dBA, 6 hours at 92, 4 hours at 95, 3 hours at 97 and 2 hours at 100 dBA (shorter durations at higher levels follow, up to 115 dBA for 1/4 hour or less).
points.quote: Duration per day, hours Sound level dBA slow response 8 90 6 92 4 95 3 97 2 100

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: In all cases where sound levels exceed the table values, a continuing, effective hearing conservation program must be administered.
points.quote: In all cases where the sound levels exceed the values shown herein, a continuing, effective hearing conservation program shall be administered.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: When daily exposure is made up of periods at different levels, the combined effect is computed with the formula Fe = (T1/L1) + (T2/L2) + ... + (Tn/Ln). If Fe exceeds unity (1), the exposure exceeds permissible levels.
points.quote: If the value of Fe exceeds unity (1) the exposure exceeds permissible levels.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level.
points.quote: Exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.52, Occupational noise exposure (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Only qualified and trained employees may be assigned to install, adjust and operate laser equipment, and proof of the operator's qualification must be available and in the operator's possession at all times.
points.quote: Only qualified and trained employees shall be assigned to install, adjust, and operate laser equipment.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.54, Nonionizing radiation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Employees in areas with a potential exposure to direct or reflected laser light greater than 0.005 watts (5 milliwatts) must be provided with antilaser eye protection devices as specified in Subpart E.
points.quote: a potential exposure to direct or reflected laser light greater than 0.005 watts (5 milliwatts) exists, shall be provided with antilaser eye protection devices as specified in subpart E of this part.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.54, Nonionizing radiation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Beam shutters or caps must be used, or the laser turned off, when laser transmission is not actually required. A laser left unattended for a substantial period (such as lunch hour, overnight or change of shifts) must be turned off.
points.quote: Beam shutters or caps shall be utilized, or the laser turned off, when laser transmission is not actually required.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.54, Nonionizing radiation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: The laser beam may not be directed at employees.
points.quote: The laser beam shall not be directed at employees.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.54, Nonionizing radiation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Employees may not be exposed to microwave power densities above 10 milliwatts per square centimeter.
points.quote: Employees shall not be exposed to microwave power densities in excess of 10 milliwatts per square centimeter.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.54, Nonionizing radiation (as of Nov 3, 2026)

topics.name: Air contaminants and ventilation

points.text: For a substance in Table 1 of 1926.55 whose limit is preceded by (C), a ceiling value, exposure measured from breathing-zone air samples must at no time exceed the limit. If instantaneous monitoring is not feasible, the employer assesses the ceiling as a 15-minute time-weighted average that may not be exceeded at any time during the working day.
points.quote: If instantaneous monitoring is not feasible, then the employer must assess the ceiling as a 15-minute time-weighted average exposure that the employer cannot exceed at any time during the working day.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.55, Gases, vapors, fumes, dusts, and mists (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: For substances in Table 1 or 2 whose limit is not preceded by (C), exposure must not exceed the limit measured as an 8-hour time-weighted average in any work shift.
points.quote: must not exceed the limit specified for that substance measured as an 8-hour time-weighted average in any work shift.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.55, Gases, vapors, fumes, dusts, and mists (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: To comply, administrative or engineering controls must first be implemented whenever feasible. When they cannot achieve full compliance, protective equipment or other protective measures are used, first approved for each particular use by a competent industrial hygienist or other technically qualified person. Respirator use must comply with 1926.103.
points.quote: administrative or engineering controls must first be implemented whenever feasible.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.55, Gases, vapors, fumes, dusts, and mists (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Paragraphs (a) and (b) of 1926.55 do not apply to airborne asbestos, tremolite, anthophyllite or actinolite dust (1926.1101 applies) or to formaldehyde (1910.1048 applies).
points.quote: Whenever any employee is exposed to airborne asbestos, tremolite, anthophyllite, or actinolite dust, the requirements of § 1926.1101 shall apply.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.55, Gases, vapors, fumes, dusts, and mists (as of Nov 3, 2026)

points.text: Whenever hazardous substances such as dusts, fumes, mists, vapors or gases exist or are produced in construction work, their concentrations may not exceed the limits in 1926.55(a). When ventilation is used as an engineering control, the system must be installed and operated according to 1926.57.
points.quote: When ventilation is used as an engineering control method, the system shall be installed and operated according to the requirements of this section.

points.text: Local exhaust ventilation must be designed to prevent dispersion of contaminants into the air in concentrations causing harmful exposure, and so that they are not drawn through the work area of employees.
points.quote: Such exhaust systems shall be so designed that dusts, fumes, mists, vapors, or gases are not drawn through the work area of employees.

points.text: The air outlet from every dust separator, and the contaminants collected by an exhaust or ventilating system, must discharge to the outside atmosphere. Systems that return air to the work area may be used only if the concentrations that build up do not result in harmful exposure.
points.quote: Collecting systems which return air to work area may be used if concentrations which accumulate in the work area air do not result in harmful exposure to employees.

topics.notCovered: The substance-by-substance limits in Tables 1 and 2 of 1926.55, and the detailed 1926.57 rules for abrasive blasting, grinding, spray finishing and open surface tanks.

points.text: Construction areas, ramps, runways, corridors, offices, shops and storage areas must be lighted to at least the minimum intensities in Table D-3 while any work is in progress.
points.quote: Construction areas, ramps, runways, corridors, offices, shops, and storage areas shall be lighted to not less than the minimum illumination intensities listed in Table D-3 while any work is in progress:

points.text: Table D-3 lists 5 foot-candles for general construction area lighting, and 3 foot-candles for general construction areas, concrete placement, excavation and waste areas, accessways, active storage areas, loading platforms, refueling and field maintenance areas.
points.quote: 3 General construction areas, concrete placement, excavation and waste areas, accessways, active storage areas, loading platforms, refueling, and field maintenance areas.

points.text: Tunnels, shafts and general underground work areas are listed at 5 foot-candles, with an exception: at least 10 foot-candles at the tunnel and shaft heading during drilling, mucking and scaling.
points.quote: minimum of 10 footcandles is required at tunnel and shaft heading during drilling, mucking, and scaling.

points.text: General construction plant and shops (such as batch plants, mechanical and electrical equipment rooms, carpenter shops, mess halls and indoor toilets) are listed at 10 foot-candles; first aid stations, infirmaries and offices at 30.
points.quote: 30 First aid stations, infirmaries, and offices.

topics.name: Hazard communication

points.text: Section 1926.59 is a note: the hazard communication requirements for construction work are identical to those in 29 CFR 1910.1200.
points.quote: The requirements applicable to construction work under this section are identical to those set forth at § 1910.1200 of this chapter.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.59, Hazard communication (as of Nov 3, 2026)

topics.notCovered: The content of 29 CFR 1910.1200 (labels, safety data sheets, training, written program and the 2024 revision's compliance dates). It has its own study guide.

topics.name: Lead

points.text: 1926.62 applies to all construction work where an employee may be occupationally exposed to lead. Construction work means work for construction, alteration and/or repair, including painting and decorating.
points.quote: This section applies to all construction work where an employee may be occupationally exposed to lead.

points.text: The action level is employee exposure, without regard to respirators, to an airborne lead concentration of 30 micrograms per cubic meter of air (30 µg/m3) calculated as an 8-hour TWA.
points.quote: Action level means employee exposure, without regard to the use of respirators, to an airborne concentration of lead of 30 micrograms per cubic meter of air (30 µg/m3) calculated as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA).

points.text: The PEL: no employee may be exposed to lead above 50 µg/m3 averaged over an 8-hour period. For work days longer than 8 hours, the allowable exposure is 400 divided by hours worked in the day.
points.quote: Allowable employee exposure (in µg/m3) = 400 divided by hours worked in the day.

points.text: For listed tasks where lead is present (for example manual scraping, manual sanding and heat gun use where lead-containing coatings or paint are present, and spray painting with lead paint), until an exposure assessment documents otherwise, the employer must treat the employee as exposed above the PEL and provide interim protection.
points.quote: the employer shall treat the employee as if the employee were exposed above the PEL, and not in excess of ten (10) times the PEL

points.text: If exposure is at or above the action level but at or below the PEL, monitoring is done at least every 6 months until at least two consecutive measurements, taken at least 7 days apart, are below the action level. If the initial determination shows exposure above the PEL, monitoring is quarterly until two such consecutive measurements are at or below the PEL but at or above the action level, and then follows the 6-month schedule (additional monitoring is required after changes under 1926.62(d)(7)).
points.quote: If the initial determination reveals that employee exposure is above the PEL the employer shall perform monitoring quarterly.

points.text: Before the job starts, each employer must establish and implement a written compliance program. It must provide for frequent and regular inspections by a competent person and be revised and updated at least annually.
points.quote: Prior to commencement of the job each employer shall establish and implement a written compliance program to achieve compliance with paragraph (c) of this section.

points.text: Where exposure is above the PEL (without regard to respirators), where employees are exposed to lead compounds that may cause skin or eye irritation, and as interim protection for the listed tasks, the employer must provide protective work clothing and equipment at no cost to the employee and make sure it is used.
points.quote: the employer shall provide at no cost to the employee and assure that the employee uses appropriate protective work clothing and equipment that prevents contamination of the employee and the employee's garments

points.text: In areas where exposure is above the PEL (without regard to respirators), food or beverage may not be present or consumed, tobacco products may not be present or used, and cosmetics may not be applied.
points.quote: food or beverage is not present or consumed, tobacco products are not present or used, and cosmetics are not applied.

points.text: Initial medical surveillance (blood lead and zinc protoporphyrin testing) is made available to employees exposed on any day at or above the action level. A full medical surveillance program is required for employees who are or may be exposed at or above the action level for more than 30 days in any consecutive 12 months, and required medical surveillance is made available without cost to employees.
points.quote: for all employees who are or may be exposed by the employer at or above the action level for more than 30 days in any consecutive 12 months;

points.text: The employer must remove an employee from work with exposure at or above the action level each time a periodic and a follow-up blood test show a blood lead level at or above 50 µg/dl. An employee removed for that reason returns to former job status when two consecutive blood tests show below 40 µg/dl.
points.quote: the employee's blood lead level is at or above 50 µg/dl;

points.text: The employer must provide up to eighteen (18) months of medical removal protection benefits each time an employee is removed from exposure to lead or otherwise limited under 1926.62.
points.quote: The employer shall provide an employee up to eighteen (18) months of medical removal protection benefits on each occasion that an employee is removed from exposure to lead or otherwise limited pursuant to this section.

points.text: The training program must be given at least annually to each employee exposed to lead at or above the action level on any day.
points.quote: The employer shall also provide the training program at least annually for each employee who is subject to lead exposure at or above the action level on any day.

topics.notCovered: The full medical examination contents, multiple physician review, recordkeeping and the appendices of 1926.62.
